title: Right adjoint of a proper flat derived pushforward commutes with direct sums
statement: Let Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let f:X\to Y be proper, flat, and of finite presentation [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism], and let a be the right adjoint to Rf_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then a commutes with all set-indexed direct sums in D_QCoh(Y).

proof.text: Since f is proper and Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so the statements about D_QCoh below apply on X as well as on Y. Let P be any perfect object of D_QCoh(X). Apply [lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image] with $E=P$ and $\mathcal G^\bullet=\mathcal O_X$ in degree 0: $\mathcal O_X$ is of finite presentation, flat over Y because f is flat, and its support X is proper over Y because f is proper; as $P\otimes^L\mathcal O_X=P$, this gives that Rf_*P is perfect on Y (Stacks 0B91 argument). By [lem-pc-perfect-object-compact] on Y it is compact. Therefore for every family (K_i) in D_QCoh(Y), the canonical map $\bigoplus_i \operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,K_i) \to \operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,\bigoplus_i K_i)$ is an isomorphism.

Let $u:\bigoplus_i a(K_i)\to a(\bigoplus_i K_i)$ be the canonical morphism induced by the coproduct inclusions and functoriality of a. Adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(P,a(\bigoplus_i K_i))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,\bigoplus_i K_i)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(P,a(K_i))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_*P,K_i)$. By [lem-pc-perfect-object-compact], P is compact, so $\operatorname{Hom}(P,\bigoplus_i a(K_i))\cong\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(P,a(K_i))$; by Step 1 and the compactness of $Rf_*P$, the resulting map to $\operatorname{Hom}(P,a(\bigoplus_i K_i))$ is an isomorphism for every perfect P.

Let C be the cone of u. By Step 2 and the long exact Hom sequence, $\operatorname{Hom}(P[n],C)=0$ for every perfect P and every $n\in\mathbf Z$. The class of A with $\operatorname{Hom}(A[n],C)=0$ for all n is closed under shifts, cones, retracts, and arbitrary direct sums, and contains all perfect objects. By [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-perfect-generation] it contains every object, hence it contains C; the identity of C is zero and C=0. Thus u is an isomorphism, so a commutes with the family of direct sums.
